scope: Six existing diagnostic cases; five sampled frames each, compared with actual PhysVid, R18E, CT and available CT noC. Not a complete motion or main40 quality pass.

cases.VP002: DT restores hand and wooden-strip content absent in early CT frames, but strip splits into multiple intersecting branches; unacceptable geometry remains.
cases.VP003: DT retains gymnast and clothes more visibly than CT but inverted body/contact and final fall are wrong; correct backhandspring not established.
cases.VP004: DT restores marked ruler and clamp instead of CT thin line, but it stays straight then develops damage without requested bend. Better object preservation is not physical-process completion.
cases.VP009: DT restores worker, suction-like tool, photo and glass. Object relation/lifting remains wrong and tool is removed by final sample.
cases.VP014: DT starts with recognizable balloons compared with CT blurred strips, but later fragments and nearly empty scene remain. Cannot certify correct burst sequence.
cases.VP015: DT still shows implausible thin floating boat, missing rower and wrong reflection. R18E has substantially more boat/person/paddle/lake content. Native-feature gating alone is insufficient here.

finding: Source-backed content and native-feature-only execution in DT recover some object/detail loss relative to CT, yet do not solve shape/process/content quality across these six. R18E remains informative for content reconstruction; no claim all R18E videos are acceptable.
causality_limit: DT versus CT changes enhancement and execution together; this comparison does not isolate either. CT/noC remains a same-checkpoint causal intervention.
